To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Advanced Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory will detect continuous gravitational waves from the Galactic population of neutron stars, with the first detection expected within the first year of Advanced LIGO operation, and that this detection will provide information about the neutron star magnetic field strength and deformation.

(i) The Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo detectors can detect continuous gravitational waves from a population of Galactic isolated neutron stars with ellipticity > 10−7 and a magnetic field strength of 10−3 G. (ii) The Advanced Ligo, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA network will detect continuous gravitational waves in the Advanced detector era from a Galactic population of neutron stars with ellipticities of ~ 10−7.
the Advanced LIGO detectors will not be able to detect continuous gravitational waves from the entire Galactic population of isolated neutron stars.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a direct gravitational-wave signal from a Galactic neutron star would have a significant impact on our understanding of neutron star physics.
a direct gravitational-wave signal from a Galactic source is unlikely, but the Advanced detector network will have an unprecedented sensitivity to continuous gravitational-wave signals.

the detection of a continuous gravitational-wave signal from a single neutron star would not be sufficient to determine the neutron star’s magnetic field strength and/or ellipticity, as the gravitational-wave signal would be degenerate with the magnetic field strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a direct detection is not required to constrain the magnetic field strength of a Galactic neutron star population.

the gravitational-wave emission from isolated neutron stars is not expected to dominate the electromagnetic emission, and thus a direct detection of gravitational waves from an isolated neutron star is unlikely.
the Advanced Detector era is the time when the Galactic neutron star community can begin to make a significant impact in gravitational-wave astronomy.
